newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita retreats after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Merita retreats after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Finnish bank group Merita turned lower in moderate trade on Thursday morning after rising earlier following in-line January-September earnings and comments on expected 1996 dividends, brokers said.

At 1150/0950 GMT, Merita's vote-strong and more liquid A share traded at 13.60 markka, down 0.20 markka or 1.4 percent, after hitting 14.20 markka in early trade. Volume was a moderate 8.8 million markka.
Merita's B share traded up 0.10 markka at 14.70, but trade was thin. The B share carries preferential right to dividend before the A share.

Brokers said investors took profits on Merita after strong recent gains as the bank's nine-month report released in the morning was in line with expectations and looked unlikely to boost the shares in the near term.
There were both domestic and overseas investors selling Merita, they said.
Merita had a 930 million markka operating profit after credit losses in January-September, up from 482 million in the first nine months in 1995.
Analysts' median forecast had been for a 952 million markka profit in an 800 million to 1.06 billion markka range.
